version.changelog: Security hardening: removed eval, inline bash from SKILL.md, moved dev tooling out of shipped dirs, gated file writes behind opt-in env var. All diagnostics route through hardened scripts requiring explicit user-provided paths.

llm.summary: The skill is mostly a local diagnostic tool, but it can read private agent logs through broad triggers and has an opt-in persistent learning write path that needs careful review.

dimensions.detail: The main runtime behavior is local file parsing with bash, jq, awk, find, and temp files; no network exfiltration, API key use, privilege escalation, or background service was found.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: install.sh performs a local copy into ~/.openclaw/skills/clawdoc and backs up an existing install; no remote installer or hidden payload retrieval was found, though the packaged artifact appears to omit some files the installer tries to copy.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md includes broad natural-language triggers such as "debug", "diagnose", "health check", and "what's wrong" while the default examples inspect OpenClaw session directories, which can contain private conversation and tool-output history.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: prescribe.sh can append or update .learnings/LEARNINGS.md when CLAWDOC_LEARNINGS=1 and a .learnings directory exists, using finding fields from caller-provided JSON without strong schema or Markdown containment.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The scripts coherently support the stated purpose of diagnosing OpenClaw/agent JSONL sessions, costs, retries, and context issues.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the agent reading local OpenClaw session logs. Prefer explicit /clawdoc commands with specific paths, avoid relying on generic natural-language triggers, and enable CLAWDOC_LEARNINGS=1 only for trusted diagnose output in repositories where persistent learning files are expected.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: .learnings persistence is documented and opt-in, so it is not hidden or malicious, but writing diagnostic content into an agent-readable learning file is a real persistence concern.
[T02] expected: The persistent write path accepts JSON from stdin, a file, or an argument and writes fields into Markdown; the feature is intended, but untrusted input could poison future learning context if users enable it.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The documented triggers are unusually generic for a shell-executing skill that reads local session logs, increasing accidental invocation risk.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill declares required binaries but does not express a narrow tool/permission scope for shell execution, so users must rely on the surrounding agent sandbox and their own invocation discipline.
[E4] expected: cost-waterfall.sh locally inspects prior tool-result text to explain cost causes; I found no code sending conversation context to an external service.
[SDI-2] unexpected: dev/convert-claude-sessions.sh can recursively delete a caller-chosen output directory after a weak prompt; this is a real but development-only utility issue and is not copied by install.sh.
[T09] unexpected: The arbitrary recursive deletion finding is supported for the dev converter script, but normal installed skill scripts do not expose that deletion path.
[RP1] expected: The npx strings are synthetic session-log content in a demo fixture, not package retrieval commands executed by the skill.
[SDI-4] expected: The changelog distinguishes current opt-in .learnings writes from prior behavior; this is documentation inconsistency at most, not evidence of hidden auto-discovery.
